:::{#exm-lik-obs}
#### Likelihood of one Bernoulli observation

If $X \sim \Ber(\prob)$, then

$$
\p_{\prob}(X = x) = \prob^x (1 - \prob)^{1 - x}
$$

for $x \in \cb{0, 1}$.
If we observe $x = 1$, the likelihood is $\Lik(\prob) = \prob$:
for example, $\Lik(0.2) = 0.2$ and $\Lik(0.7) = 0.7$,
so the observation $x = 1$ is more likely under $\prob = 0.7$
than under $\prob = 0.2$.
:::
